decision: Deepen existing 4.4.1, 5.1.2 and 5.2.1, lab 5-1 and figure 5-1 with bank demand and layout handoff; no new section/lab/figure or benchmark claim.
findings: Section II separates tiling/order/parallelism/shape from physical layout. Equal aggregate storage width can still produce different per-bank port demands. This adds a service constraint after the existing capacity/traffic calculation.

Section II-D assumes fixed inference weights can be reordered offline; activations are generated online. This premise is not a general statement about dynamic expert placement, training weights or all current framework runners.

Sections II-E and IV generate output in a layout usable by the next layer during reduction. Avoiding a separate reorder also relies on compatible dataflow selection and output write-port demand; it is not arbitrary conversion at zero hardware or control cost.

Sections III and VI describe an INT8/INT32 accelerator, temporal/spatial reduction, dedicated BIRRD, multiple SRAM banks, ping-pong storage and offline routing configuration. Routing may fall back to brute-force configuration search. No claim that an existing GPU implements BIRRD.
Section VI searches per-layer EDP within chosen layout/dataflow spaces; the FPGA deployment simplifies to two chosen layouts. This does not prove a globally optimal modern LLM graph schedule.

Figure 12 reports throughput normalized by PE count and clock, from different real/emulated platforms. It is not unnormalized whole-model GPU speedup or a fixed-resource comparison of current chips. Some layers favor DPU owing to controller overhead despite similar steady PE utilization.

Table IV changes original design dimensions/precision and lists different on-chip bandwidths. Preserve its printed 8000 bit/cycle FEATHER entry and other bandwidths without guessing a correction; these are modified modeled systems, not vendor product specifications.

Section V-B prints max(N_P/N_L,1) as a slowdown. With more lines than ports it yields 1, contradicting the stated stall interpretation and Figure 4. Do not copy this formula as a latency multiplier; use independent per-bank service counting. No source-code claim about the actual implementation.

Figure 12 labels Edge TPU comparison 4.56x, while VI-B3 says 4.91x. Retain discrepancy; neither number is adopted. Figure 4 layout labels and examples are schematic; the book uses its own explicit address map, not a digitized performance curve.

reused_document.interpretation: 32 banks of successive 32-bit words support the scalar teaching model. Documented TMA swizzle is a distinct 16-byte-chunk mapping with alignment/shape requirements, not the teaching pitch-padding formula. The official example explicitly says it is not performant or scalable as-is.
